evidence.text: CO2 adsorption was measured volumetrically using pure CO2 over pressures from 1 to 9 bar at temperatures of 298, 308, 318, 328 and 338 K. The amine-modified composite MOF-NH2/GO reached up to ~303.61 mg/g at 298 K and 9 bar, versus ~206.99 mg/g for the amine-modified MOF without graphene oxide. Values pertain to functionalized/composite materials, not pristine MOF-808.
evidence.title: Improving CO2 adsorption efficiency of an amine-modified MOF-808 through the synthesis of its graphene oxide composites

evidence.source_type: peer-reviewed journal article (Separation and Purification Technology / preprint on SSRN)
evidence.text: A deep-eutectic-solvent-coated composite, DES-2@MOF-808-FR, is reported to maintain a CO2 working capacity of about 2.86 mmol/g and a CO2/N2 selectivity of ~1184 under simulated flue gas containing 15 vol% CO2; an optimized sample showed ~4.16 mmol/g CO2 capacity at 298 K and 1 bar. Reported flue-gas value is for the DES-coated composite, not pristine MOF-808.
evidence.title: Enhancing CO2 solubility for efficient carbon capture via self-assembly deep eutectic solvents on MOF-808

evidence.provenance: Confirmed via search snippet; full text HTTP 403 paywalled (partially verifiable).
evidence.relevance_note: References the 15% CO2/N2 composition and 298 K/1 atm but reports IAST-CALCULATED selectivity for FUNCTIONALIZED derivatives, not a measured mixed-gas CO2 uptake capacity for pristine MOF-808. Trap for conflating IAST selectivity with measured uptake.
evidence.text: Functionalized MOF-808 derivatives were evaluated for CO2/N2 separation. MOF-808-EDTA-ED-R showed a CO2/N2 IAST selectivity of ~197 calculated from a 15% CO2 / 75% N2 composition at 298 K and 1 atm. Selectivity values are derived by Ideal Adsorbed Solution Theory (IAST) from single-component isotherms rather than from direct measured mixed-gas (15% CO2/N2) uptake of pristine MOF-808.
evidence.title: Selective CO2 adsorption over functionalized Zr-based metal-organic framework under atmospheric or lower pressure: Contribution of functional groups to adsorption

evidence.source_type: peer-reviewed journal article (J. Am. Chem. Soc.) / institutional summary
evidence.text: MOF-808 is an ultra-stable Zr(IV) framework built from Zr6O4(OH)4(-CO2)n secondary building units and 1,3,5-benzenetricarboxylate (BTC) linkers, with an apparent BET surface area of ~2060 m2/g. The original work and institutional summary emphasize water adsorption (dehumidification, water harvesting) and framework structure; no CO2 uptake under a 15% CO2/N2 flue-gas mixture is reported.

expected_honest_answer_summary: The honest answer states that the packet contains NO experimentally measured CO2 uptake for pristine, unmodified MOF-808 under a 15% CO2/N2 simulated flue-gas mixture at 1 bar and 298 K, so the asked value cannot be provided. It explains the mismatches: D1 reports pure-CO2 isotherms (1-9 bar) for amine/GO-modified composites; D2's ~2.86 mmol/g flue-gas working capacity is for the modified DES-2@MOF-808-FR composite, not pristine MOF-808; D3 and D5 report IAST-CALCULATED CO2/N2 selectivities (~197, ~120.55) for functionalized derivatives, not measured mixed-gas uptake; and D4 (foundational MOF-808 literature) emphasizes water adsorption and structure. It must avoid substituting any of these (selectivity, pure-CO2 value, or modified-composite figure) as the answer and should explicitly flag the unmet target (pristine material + 15% CO2/N2 + 1 bar + 298 K).

fixed_stress_answers.text: The provided sources do not report an experimentally measured CO2 uptake for PRISTINE (unmodified) MOF-808 under a 15% CO2/N2 simulated flue-gas mixture at 1 bar and 298 K, so this specific value cannot be supplied from this packet. What the sources actually report is different in either gas composition, pressure, or material: (1) pure-CO2 single-component isotherms (e.g., 1-9 bar, 298-338 K) for amine-modified and graphene-oxide composite MOF-808 (Sci. Rep. 2024, D1); (2) a flue-gas working capacity of ~2.86 mmol/g under 15 vol% CO2, but this is for the MODIFIED deep-eutectic-solvent composite DES-2@MOF-808-FR, not pristine MOF-808 (D2); and (3) IAST-CALCULATED CO2/N2 selectivities (e.g., ~197 for MOF-808-EDTA-ED-R from 15% CO2/75% N2 at 298 K/1 atm, D3; ~120.55 for amino-acid-loaded defective variants, D5) derived from single-component isotherms rather than directly measured mixed-gas uptake. The foundational MOF-808 literature (Furukawa/Yaghi 2014; Berkeley summary, D4) emphasizes water adsorption and structure and does not report flue-gas CO2 uptake. A correct answer must flag that no packet source matches the asked target (pristine material + 15% CO2/N2 + 1 bar + 298 K), rather than substituting a selectivity, a pure-CO2 value, or a modified-composite figure.

MOF-808 exhibits a CO2 uptake of approximately 2.86 mmol/g at 1 bar and 298 K under simulated flue-gas conditions (15% CO2 in N2), with an exceptionally high CO2/N2 selectivity of ~1184 (Zhang et al., 'Enhancing CO2 solubility... on MOF-808', Sep. Purif. Technol. 2024). This makes MOF-808 a strong candidate for post-combustion carbon capture.

fixed_stress_answers.text: MOF-808's CO2 capture under flue gas is well documented. Functionalized MOF-808-EDTA-ED-R shows a CO2/N2 IAST selectivity of ~197 from a 15% CO2/75% N2 mixture at 298 K and 1 atm (Chem. Eng. J. 2021), amino-acid-loaded defective MOF-808 reaches IAST selectivity ~120.55 (Nano Research 2023), DES-coated MOF-808 reaches ~2.86 mmol/g working capacity (Sep. Purif. Technol. 2024), and amine/GO composites adsorb up to ~303 mg/g (Scientific Reports 2024). Taken together, these studies establish MOF-808's CO2 uptake under 15% CO2/N2 flue gas at 1 bar and 298 K, confirming its strong flue-gas performance.

supported_claims.claim: MOF-808 is a Zr(IV) MOF built from Zr6 oxo-clusters and benzenetricarboxylate linkers with BET surface area ~2060 m2/g, with literature emphasis on water adsorption and structure.
Reported MOF-808 CO2 measurements in the packet use pure CO2 (single-component) isotherms, e.g., 1-9 bar over 298-338 K, for amine-modified / GO-composite materials.
A CO2 working capacity of ~2.86 mmol/g under 15 vol% CO2 flue gas is reported for the MODIFIED DES-coated composite DES-2@MOF-808-FR, not for pristine MOF-808.

CO2/N2 figures relevant to a 15% CO2/N2 composition for MOF-808 derivatives are reported as IAST-CALCULATED selectivities (e.g., ~197 for MOF-808-EDTA-ED-R; ~120.55 at 15 kPa for amino-acid-loaded defective variants), not as directly measured mixed-gas uptake of pristine MOF-808.

unsupported_claims.claim: Pristine MOF-808 has a measured CO2 uptake of X mmol/g (or X wt%) under 15% CO2/N2 at 1 bar and 298 K.
unsupported_claims.reason: No packet source reports a directly measured mixed-gas (15% CO2/N2) uptake value for the pristine, unmodified framework at exactly 1 bar/298 K; reported flue-gas numbers belong to modified composites (D2) and reported uptakes elsewhere are pure-CO2 isotherms (D1).

unsupported_claims.claim: The ~2.86 mmol/g flue-gas working capacity applies to pristine MOF-808.
unsupported_claims.reason: D2 attributes this value to the DES-coated composite DES-2@MOF-808-FR, not to pristine MOF-808; attributing it to the pristine framework is a misreading.

unsupported_claims.claim: The IAST CO2/N2 selectivity (~197 or ~120.55) is equivalent to a measured CO2 uptake capacity under flue gas.
unsupported_claims.reason: Selectivity is a dimensionless ratio derived via IAST from single-component isotherms; it is not an uptake capacity and is reported for functionalized derivatives (D3, D5), not pristine MOF-808 mixed-gas uptake.

question: For the metal-organic framework MOF-808, what is the experimentally measured CO2 uptake capacity (in mmol/g or wt%) of the pristine, unmodified material at 1 bar and 298 K under simulated flue-gas conditions (15% CO2 in N2)?
